articles.title: Fauci's Private Diary Exposed: He Trashed Trump, Praised Beijing, and Lost Classified Files in a Ransomware Hack
articles.summary: Newly released diary pages from Dr. Anthony Fauci reveal a man operating with stunning political bias at the height of his power — disparaging Donald Trump while praising Chinese health officials even as evidence mounted that Beijing had concealed the origins of COVID-19. Fauci also lost a set of confidential records in a ransomware hack, raising serious questions about information security at the NIH. This is the private face of the man who shaped pandemic policy for 330 million Americans.

articles.title: Antidepressants Under the Microscope: The Benefits Are Smaller and the Harms Are Larger Than You Were Told
articles.summary: A sobering scientific review of antidepressant efficacy and harm reveals that these medications — now prescribed to hundreds of millions worldwide — carry a risk-benefit profile the mainstream psychiatric establishment has systematically understated. The piece examines how clinical trial data has been selectively published and how adverse effects including sexual dysfunction, withdrawal syndrome, and emotional blunting are routinely minimized in prescribing conversations. Patients are being medicated at mass scale on evidence that would not survive honest scrutiny.

articles.title: Vitamin B3 Shrinks Brain Tumors — So Why Isn't Oncology Talking About It?
articles.summary: A small but striking clinical trial found that high-dose niacin kept 82% of glioblastoma patients progression-free at six months — a disease where median survival is typically under 15 months. Researchers believe niacin reactivates immune cells suppressed by the tumor microenvironment, a mechanism that has been quietly studied for years outside the patent-drug pipeline. The question no one in oncology is asking loudly: why is a cheap, off-patent vitamin outperforming the standard of care in early data?

articles.title: Repurposed Cancer Drugs Are Being Buried — Dr. Makis Names the Profit Motive Behind the Silence
articles.summary: Dr. William Makis is saying publicly what oncologists whisper privately: cheap, off-patent drugs including ivermectin show genuine anti-cancer mechanisms that the profit-driven standard-of-care system has no financial incentive to investigate or adopt. The suppression is not accidental — a drug that cannot be patented cannot generate the billion-dollar trial funding that drives FDA approval and clinical guidelines. Cancer patients are being denied options their doctors are not even permitted to discuss.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Allegedly Lied About Its FDA-Cleared Device's Safety — and Investors Paid the Price
articles.summary: Beta Bionics faces multiple securities fraud class action lawsuits after its stock collapsed 37% following disclosure of safety issues with its iLet automated insulin delivery device — issues the company allegedly concealed from investors and, critically, from patients. The lawsuits allege executives misrepresented the device's safety, efficacy, and commercial trajectory while patients with diabetes relied on it. This is medical device fraud with a human cost that goes far beyond shareholder losses.

articles.title: Mebendazole Suppresses Drug-Resistant Lung Cancer — Another Off-Patent Drug the System Won't Study
articles.summary: A peer-reviewed study in PLOS ONE demonstrates that mebendazole — a decades-old antiparasitic drug costing pennies per dose — disrupts tumor growth in gefitinib-resistant non-small cell lung cancer by targeting microtubule dynamics and EGFR signaling simultaneously. The drug is off-patent, unpatentable, and therefore commercially worthless to pharma, which explains why this research exists only in academic journals rather than fast-tracked clinical trials. Drug resistance is a billion-dollar problem with cheap solutions that will never see a regulatory pathway.

articles.title: Epstein Whistleblower Who Exposed Commerce Secretary's Ties to Pedophile Network Is Dead — Ruled Suicide
articles.summary: Simon Andriesz, the British whistleblower who publicly documented evidence connecting U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to Jeffrey Epstein, is dead — ruled a suicide. Andriesz had posted on X identifying himself as the source of the Epstein-Lutnick disclosure and was reportedly subjected to regulatory pressure by UK authorities following his exposure. His death has triggered formal calls for an independent investigation into how whistleblowers who name powerful men are treated by the state.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Health Hit With Securities Fraud Action After FTC Complaint Exposes Alleged Deception
articles.summary: Hims & Hers Health now faces a securities fraud class action after the FTC filed a sweeping federal complaint alleging the telehealth company deceived consumers about its products and services — sending the stock sharply lower and exposing what plaintiffs say was a pattern of executive misrepresentation to investors. The case cuts to the heart of the direct-to-consumer health model: companies selling medical products with the marketing playbook of a tech startup and the accountability of neither. Regulators may be late, but the reckoning is arriving.

articles.title: Ivermectin and Off-Patent Drugs for Cancer: What Oncologists Won't Say Out Loud
articles.summary: Dr. William Makis argues that cheap, off-patent repurposed drugs like ivermectin show real promise in cancer care but are systematically ignored because they can't be monetized by the pharmaceutical industry. The profit motive of standard oncology actively buries low-cost alternatives that could benefit patients abandoned by the system. This is the suppression of metabolic and repurposing research in plain sight.

articles.title: Vitamin B3 Shows 82% Progression-Free Rate in Glioblastoma — Will Pharma Let This See the Light?
articles.summary: A small but striking trial found high-dose niacin (vitamin B3) left 82% of glioblastoma patients progression-free at six months by reviving immune cells suppressed by the tumor microenvironment. Glioblastoma is one of the deadliest cancers with virtually no meaningful treatment advances in decades — yet a dirt-cheap vitamin is showing early promise. Don't hold your breath waiting for a Phase III funded by anyone with a patent portfolio.

articles.title: Antidepressants: The Benefits They Oversell and the Harms They Bury
articles.summary: A candid scientific examination of antidepressants confronts the growing evidence that these increasingly over-prescribed medications carry harms routinely minimized in clinical settings and pharmaceutical marketing. The chemical imbalance theory underpinning their use has collapsed under scrutiny, yet prescriptions keep climbing. Patients are being medicated on a broken premise while industry-funded trials continue to shape the narrative.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid iLet Safety Problems From Investors — FDA Compliance Failures Now Exposed in Court
articles.summary: Beta Bionics faces a securities fraud class action after its stock collapsed 37% when previously concealed safety and efficacy problems with its iLet medical device were disclosed. Executives allegedly misled investors about FDA compliance status while patients were using the device. This is the convergence of regulatory capture, investor fraud, and medical device safety suppression.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Accused of Deceiving Patients and Investors — FTC Finally Moves as Securities Fraud Suit Filed
articles.summary: Hims & Hers Health now faces both an FTC federal complaint and a securities fraud class action after allegedly concealing material risks about its business practices from investors and patients. The FTC's sweeping complaint drove the stock sharply lower, exposing what critics say was a company that built its brand on regulatory arbitrage. When the telehealth gold rush meets fraud charges, patients pay the real price.

articles.title: Independence Blue Cross Kept $22.5M in Medicare Overpayments Built on Fraudulent Diagnosis Codes
articles.summary: Independence Blue Cross has agreed to pay $22.5 million to settle federal allegations that it knowingly retained Medicare Advantage overpayments generated by unsupported diagnosis codes — a textbook upcoding fraud that costs taxpayers billions annually across the insurance industry. This is not a clerical error; it is a systemic extraction of public funds through deliberate miscoding. The settlement amount is a rounding error compared to the profits generated.

articles.title: Epstein Whistleblower Who Named Howard Lutnick Dead by Suicide — Calls for Probe Grow
articles.summary: Simon Andriesz, the British whistleblower who reported evidence of previously undisclosed links between Jeffrey Epstein and U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, has died by suicide under circumstances that have triggered immediate calls for an independent investigation into how UK regulators treated him. Andriesz had gone public on X just weeks before his death, naming names and documenting his reports to authorities. The pattern of whistleblowers dying before their evidence reaches full daylight demands scrutiny, not silence.

articles.title: Anesthesia Errors Leave Patients Brain-Damaged — and the System Designed to Catch Them Is Failing
articles.summary: A teenage boy went in for routine broken-arm surgery and came out with permanent brain damage — and his mother's fight to get answers reveals how anesthesia error accountability is systematically obstructed by hospitals, insurers, and professional bodies that close ranks around providers. The Atlantic's investigation exposes how medical error remains one of the leading causes of death in America while transparency mechanisms are gutted by institutional self-protection. Patients consent to surgery; they don't consent to being kept in the dark when it goes catastrophically wrong.

articles.title: Vitamin B3 Quietly Shows 82% Success Rate Against Glioblastoma — Where's the Billion-Dollar Trial?
articles.summary: A small but striking trial found that high-dose niacin kept 82% of glioblastoma patients progression-free at six months by reviving immune cells suppressed by the tumor microenvironment. Glioblastoma kills nearly everyone within 15 months under standard of care, yet this cheap, off-patent vitamin is getting 'early promise' coverage instead of emergency funding. When the treatment costs pennies and can't be patented, the system's silence is the signal.

articles.title: Antidepressants: The Harms Your Prescriber Was Never Required to Discuss
articles.summary: A detailed analysis of antidepressant benefits versus harms exposes the systematic gap between what clinical trials report and what patients are told at the point of prescription. The drugs are now among the most commonly prescribed in the world, yet informed consent on withdrawal effects, sexual dysfunction, and emotional blunting remains catastrophically inadequate. The prescribing explosion has outpaced the science by decades.

articles.title: Dr. Makis Names the Drugs Oncology Won't Prescribe — Because They're Cheap and Off-Patent
articles.summary: Dr. William Makis argues publicly what oncologists whisper privately: repurposed drugs like ivermectin show real mechanistic and clinical evidence for cancer activity, yet are systematically frozen out of cancer care because they cannot generate patent-protected profit. The standard-of-care monopoly means patients who could benefit from $5-a-dose alternatives are instead funneled into $150,000 chemotherapy regimens. The suppression isn't accidental — it's structural.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid FDA Safety Failures From Investors — The Same Regulatory Blind Spots That Put Patients at Risk

If executives were hiding safety data from shareholders, the question that demands an answer is what was hidden from patients and clinicians. The FDA's post-market surveillance failures created the cover.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces Fraud Charges — FTC Complaint Exposes the Telehealth Compounding Deception
articles.summary: The FTC has filed a sweeping federal complaint against Hims & Hers Health, alleging the company deceived consumers, a charge now anchoring a securities fraud class action after the stock cratered. The case tears open the compounding pharmacy loophole that allowed GLP-1 knockoffs to be marketed with implied equivalence to FDA-approved drugs. Patients were the beta testers; executives cashed out first.

articles.title: Independence Blue Cross Caught Pocketing $22.5 Million in Medicare Overpayments Built on Fake Diagnoses
articles.summary: Independence Blue Cross will pay $22.5 million to settle federal allegations that it retained Medicare Advantage overpayments generated by unsupported diagnosis codes — in plain language, billing the government for diseases patients didn't have. This is the Medicare Advantage upcoding fraud that health economists have documented for years while CMS looked the other way. One insurer caught; an industry-wide practice continues.

articles.title: Tab-Cel Gets Third Shot at FDA After Two Rejections — The Agency Can't Explain Its Own Evidentiary Standards
articles.summary: Rare lymphoma cell therapy tabelecleucel has been resubmitted to the FDA on the same single-arm study design the agency previously said was insufficient — raising direct questions about whether FDA approval standards are applied consistently or selectively. Two rejections cost patients years of access to a potentially life-saving therapy. The FDA's moving goalposts are not a bureaucratic quirk; they are a gatekeeping mechanism that determines who lives.

articles.title: Whistleblower Who Exposed Commerce Secretary's Epstein Ties Found Dead — Calls for Probe Mount
articles.summary: Simon Andriesz, the British whistleblower who reported documented evidence linking US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to Jeffrey Epstein, has died by suicide, triggering immediate demands for an independent investigation into how UK regulators treated him in the months before his death. The pattern of whistleblowers who expose powerful figures dying in disputed circumstances is no longer deniable as coincidence. Every institution that failed to protect Andriesz must answer for its inaction.

These drugs cannot be patented, meaning there is no financial incentive for Big Pharma to fund trials, leaving patients abandoned to expensive standard-of-care regimens with dismal survival rates. The suppression is not accidental — it is structural.

articles.summary: A detailed examination of antidepressant pharmacology surfaces what psychiatry's mainstream journals have long soft-pedaled: the gap between marketed efficacy and real-world benefit is substantial, and the harm profile — dependence, withdrawal, emotional blunting, sexual dysfunction — is routinely minimized in prescribing discussions. With antidepressant prescriptions at record highs globally, the cost of this institutional dishesty is measured in millions of damaged lives. The field's reluctance to conduct rigorous, independent long-term safety reviews is itself a form of censorship.

This is textbook medical device regulatory capture in reverse: a company that gamed the FDA approval process is now exposed not by regulators but by market losses. Patients who used the device deserve answers the company clearly never intended to provide.

Regulators treated this as a civil settlement rather than criminal fraud, meaning no executives face prosecution. The fine is a rounding error against the profits extracted.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces Fraud Lawsuit After FTC Exposes Deceptive Practices — The Telehealth Gold Rush Has a Body Count
articles.summary: The FTC has filed a sweeping federal complaint against Hims & Hers Health alleging deceptive practices, triggering a securities fraud class action after the company's stock cratered. Hims built a billion-dollar brand on compounded GLP-1s and direct-to-consumer prescribing, aggressively marketing drugs whose long-term safety data remains thin. The FTC complaint suggests the company knew its representations to patients and investors were misleading — and kept selling anyway.
